- Overestimate prices when sentiment is bullish (sentiment > 0.5) and especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (sentiment < 0.3) or after prolonged bearish streaks; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Avoid lagging the true price by more than 2–3 days; if forecast is delayed, adjust upward by 1–2% per day lag.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., >7% from prior day) — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), forecast should be closer to historical mean of last 7–10 days; avoid extreme deviations.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–4% to avoid overcorrection.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is trending upward, allow 1–2% higher than 30d average; if downward, allow 1–2% lower.
